rules_sent_back.instruction: When The description describes a repeating activity (for example, measuring continuously) that resumes after an interruption, and a monitored condition (for example, a lost connection or a measurement crossing a limit) ends the whole process while the repetition otherwise continues.: Model the repeating flow with a decision point where the monitored condition is checked. Connect the branch in which the condition holds to its own terminal path, and end that path with an explicit end event. If the description attaches a further action to the ending, place that action as a task before the end event. The repeating flow must keep its own exit, so the process has at least one explicit end event and no loop is left without a way out.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description describes a repeating activity (for example, measuring continuously) that resumes after an interruption, and a monitored condition (for example, a lost connection or a measurement crossing a limit) ends the whole process while the repetition otherwise continues.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an occurrence which can happen at any moment while the running process is active (for example a monitored device losing its connection) stops the whole process, and that occurrence does not start the process: Model the occurrence as an interrupting event subprocess (triggeredByEvent=true) in the scope of the main process. It has exactly one triggered start event, and that start event leads to a terminate end event, so the whole process stops. Do not model the occurrence as a regular expanded subprocess with an ordinary start event, do not model it as a start event of the process, and do not model it as a receive task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an occurrence which can happen at any moment while the running process is active (for example a monitored device losing its connection) stops the whole process, and that occurrence does not start the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When The description says a metric is computed from several measured components, each of which is obtained from an external system before the calculation step.: Model the retrieval of each component as its own bpmn:serviceTask that calls the external system, placed before the calculation task. Do not fold several component retrievals into a single receiveTask or other single task.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description says a metric is computed from several measured components, each of which is obtained from an external system before the calculation step.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that one step requires several concurrent activities or several parties to be handled together, and a later point is described as needing all of them finished or available: Model each concurrent activity or party as its own branch after a parallel gateway fork, with its own task or event in each branch, and close the branches with a parallel gateway join before the later point. Do not collapse the branches into one activity, do not let a single branch continue alone, and do not use an exclusive gateway for a join where every branch must complete.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that one result must be derived from several pieces of information that can be gathered independently of each other, and the derivation is described only after all of them are available

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a person performs a named action on a monitored device (such as restarting, repairing or disconnecting it) and the flow then continues or ends, and the description does not state that the process waits for an external message, signal, time or condition for that action: Model each such person-performed action as a manual task named after the action the person performs, on the branch where it occurs, placed before the step that continues or ends the flow. Do not model it as an intermediate catch event, a start event, or an expanded subprocess. Use an intermediate catch event or an event-based gateway only where the description states that the process waits for an external message, signal, time or condition.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a person performs a named action on a monitored device (such as restarting, repairing or disconnecting it) and the flow then continues or ends, and the description does not state that the process waits for an external message, signal, time or condition for that action

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that after an interruption of a repeated activity (for example, a stopped device is brought back online), the same repeated activity must continue measuring: Model the continuation as a task placed after the step that ended the interruption, and connect it with a sequence flow back into the gateway that starts each cycle of the repeated activity. Do not model the continuation as a new start event or as a separate process, so the repetition keeps its loop and its existing entry point.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that after an interruption of a repeated activity (for example, a stopped device is brought back online), the same repeated activity must continue measuring
